kvarner.note:
Nine households of the name on the Kvarner, from 1626 to 1855, in two towns twelve kilometres apart. **None of them is joined to another by a record.** They are **not, however, farmers**: the Hungarian state records name a harbour master of Fiume, a draughtsman who drew the imperial salt office at Bakar in 1827, and two naval officers of the name. They are set out in the order the register produced them, with the broken rungs marked for what they are — the places where a join looks likely and is not written down. Read the mothers' surnames with care: on four of these the indexer has copied the father's name into the mother's field, which is why so many of these men appear to have married a woman of their own name.

**28 September 2026 — what the plate gave that the index could not, and it is mostly Valentino's household.**

*The cards below were built from the FamilySearch index. **Fourteen searches in September went to the film itself**, and they are the reason the Valentino household has ten children and five burials rather than a handful of index rows.*

· **The household is ours, and a plate settled it.** *The index writes the surname a dozen ways at Fiume; the register page writes «**de Franceschi**», and that is what the cards now carry.*
· **Four dates no index reaches.** *St Vitus baptisms, film **005497925**, read at four openings the index does not cover — including **23 November 1772** and **12 July 1774**, where the godfather is **Ignatio Defranceschi**, a man the index never produced at all.*
· **1757 was a bad year.** *A baptism under «Die 21 July 1757» and a burial in September, entry 14 — **Maria's**, which is the entry that raised the question Aloysia's answered.* **Five of Valentino's ten children were buried.**
· **They kept company above their station.** *At one font stands **the wife of the Captain of Kastav** — which is not where a labouring household's godparents come from, and is the single strongest hint that this family was not what the card's bare names suggest.*
· **And the marriage register was found in the same film**, *which is what item 143 needs to close: it would give each of these men a father and each bride a family.*

**⚠ None of this joins the nine households to each other.** *That is still true, and it is the honest state of the Kvarner: **nine households, 1626 to 1855, in two towns twelve kilometres apart, and not one record joining any two of them.***

cards.says: The oldest household the archive holds anywhere. Six children at Rijeka under a Venetian-Latin hand — *Gioannis Antonÿ*, with the trema the scribe put there. This one has been read on the page.

**Ten children, and five of them buried in the year they were born.** Mattio and Nicolò both dead in 1742, Antonio dead 1 September 1753, Aloysia dead 14 September 1757, Maria dead in the same year. The five without dates are the baptisms; the five with them are the burials. This is what a mid-century Kvarner household actually looked like in the register.

rung.text: **A hundred and ten years with nothing in them.** Between Lutia's last child in 1632 and Valentino's first in 1742 the index holds no Defranceschi at Rijeka at all. Whether these are one family across four unrecorded generations or two arrivals a century apart, nothing here can say.

cards.says: Four children, and the index has entered the eldest twice — once from his baptism on 22 November 1772 and once from his burial on 22 August 1775. **Valentino, named for the man fathering at Rijeka thirty years earlier, died at two years and nine months.** The second Ellena, born 1775, was dead by 2 March 1776; the first, born 11 July 1774, is not in the burial book.

rung.text: Giuseppe naming his first son **Valentino** in 1772, when a Valentino was fathering in the same town in 1742–57, is the ordinary grandfather-to-grandson pattern. It is the best reason to think these two households are one family — and it is a naming habit, not a record.

kids.name: Franciscum Josephum Aloysium Joannem Nepomuc Defranceschi
Antonium Petrum Nataliem Joannem Kepomuc Defranceschi

cards.says: **Twelve children in eleven years**, and nine of them carry *Nepomucena* or *Nepomuc* — John of Nepomuk, the Bohemian saint the Habsburgs pushed hard through their new lands. A family naming every child for the dynasty's saint, in the Hungarian crown's free port, is not a peasant household. Three died small: Giosefa in 1797, Anna in 1800, Maria in 1804.

rung.text: The obvious chain would run Valentino → Giuseppe → Valentino. **It does not close.** The one boy who could carry it, Giuseppe's Valentino, was buried in 1775, nineteen years before this household begins. If this Valentino is Giuseppe's son he is a later one, born after 1775, and no record of him has been found.

cards.says: Two entries, one child — Pietro Paolo, baptised and buried in the same year. The surname has lost its prefix: *Franceschi*, not *Defranceschi*, in both hands.
The name moves twelve kilometres down the coast to Bakar, written in the registers by its Latin name *Vitipolis*. Ludovicus, born 1836, lived to 1 June 1855 and died at nineteen.

rung.text: Rijeka and Bakar are one bay apart and shared a diocese, and the name appears at Bakar only after it thins at Rijeka. **Nothing joins them.** The Bakar books have not been read.

cards.says: **Twins, and a week that took two children.** Anna Francisca Catharina and Franciscus Andreas were both baptised on 10 November 1849. Carolo was buried on the 14th and Anna on the 17th. The father is entered as *Francisci Defranceschi **Regii*** — of the king — which in the Hungarian free port means an office, not a farm — and the Hungarian state's own pension rolls name a **Defranceschi Ferencz, harbour master of Fiume**, retired 1857 after forty-two years; and he is married to a second Bellinich, Carolina, where the 1836 household names Catharina.

rung.text: *Franciscus × Catharina Bellinich* in 1836 and *Francisci Regii × Carolinæ Bellinich* in 1849 are almost certainly **one man and two sisters** — the widower marrying his wife's sister. **And the office is no longer a guess.** The Hungarian parliamentary pension schedule of 1872 names **Defranceschi Ferencz, révkapitány — harbour master — of the Fiume Maritime Authority**, with 42 years and 10 months of service and a pension from 1857. *Ferencz* is Franciscus. Forty-three years back from 1857 puts him in state service by about 1814, which makes him the right age to be fathering at Bakar in 1836 and 1849.

cards.says: Two daughters, Maria Dorothea and Antonia, with no year on either in the index. **The Bakar death book now dates one of them.** On **9 March** of a year the page does not head (by its place in the book, **1775**: *inf*) the children's list has «*Antonia Gospodina Ivana / Defranceschi*», a child of «Mr Ivan Defranceschi» (*doc*, read at full size and at level 13 on 4 November 2026). That the Antonia of the register is the Antonia of this household is *inf*: the same given name, the same surname, the same town and the same decade, and *Ivan* is *Joannes*. It would put the household at Bakar **before March 1775**, and it would be the same couple as the Fiume *Joannes Baptista* who married *Catharina de Benzoni* in December 1771 ([the second Fiume household](/fiume-1626/#jbaptista)): also *inf*, on two given names and a date, with no record that names the two places together. **A second Defranceschi stands in the same death book ten years later:** «*Maria Anna Defranceschi*», an adult, between 26 and 29 May 1785, no day of her own, no husband, no age (*doc*). Nothing says who she was.

rung.text: The Bakar death book gives this household its first date: a child, *Antonia*, buried on 9 March 1775. It does not name the mother, and it calls the father *Ivan*, not *Ivan Krstitelj*.

kvarner.missing:
Two books and a third thing. **The Rijeka marriage register** would give each of these men a father and a bride's family, and would close or break the Valentino chain in an afternoon. **The Bakar baptisms** would say whether Franciscus of 1836 and Francisci Regii of 1849 are one man. Neither has been read by this archive; both survive.

**And now a third, which is open and free and merely unworked.** Hungaricana holds **196 entries for Julius Defranceschi** in the k. u. k. navy rank lists between 1894 and 1909 — a complete officer's career, ship by ship and rank by rank, that nobody has yet sat down and transcribed. It also holds Ferencz's pension schedule, Francziska's twelve years of state charity, and Anton's 1827 plan of the Bakar salt office. That is a week's honest work on material that costs nothing.

officials.heading: And what the Hungarian state records say they did
officials.note:
Fiume and Bakar were **Hungarian crown land**, not Austrian and not Croatian, so the men who held office there are in Hungarian paperwork. This archive never looked until 13 September 2026. Everything below is documented, and none of it was here yesterday.

**One caution, and it opens a door.** The 1888 account names Gentile Marussig as the orphan of a *«volt **fiumei** révkapitány»* — a former harbour master **of Fiume** — and in the very next line names Francziska Defranceschi as the orphan of a *révkapitány* with **no port given**. So Ferencz's post is placed by his authority and not by his town. The Fiume Maritime Authority governed the whole Hungarian Littoral, **Bakar included** — which means his port may have been Bakar itself, where the name is fathering in 1836 and 1849.

**28 September 2026 — and one of these men may have a pier.** *Rijeka's main harbour contains **«De Francescijev gat»**, the former **Mol Zichy** — 150 metres of stone on its east face, the pier where the port's first iron-and-concrete warehouse went up in 1882 and where **the first electric light in Rijeka was switched on**. **No source says which De Franceschi it honours.** [The full account is on /namesakes/](/namesakes/), and the question now has [worklist 157](/worklist/) behind it.*

**⚠ Ferencz is the obvious candidate and that is exactly the danger.** *A **port captain of the Fiume Maritime Authority** is the right office in the right harbour in the right century — and **not one document has yet been found joining him to the pier**. It is recorded here as a question, not an answer.*

rows.who: Joannes Baptista de Franceski
rows.what: **Died at Crikvenica as «*Perillustris Dominus* Joannes Baptista de Franceski, *Substitutus Castellanus totius Vinodol, et Officialis Cameralis*»** — deputy castellan of the whole Vinodol and an officer of the Chamber, the crown's treasury administration. The entry is a bare line: no age, no parents, no wife, no house, no priest named for the sacraments, only that he was buried in the cemetery. The surname is written **de Franceski**, with the particle and with the *-ski* ending that this archive's own Crikvenica family writes from the 1860s, and the title is a public office again, as on the rest of this page. **Two years earlier a man of the same names stands at Draga as a godfather, with an office on this coast.** In the baptism register of Draga (FamilySearch, waypoint 9R28-PTY, image 19, right page, folio 16) the entry of **21 March 1799**, a baptism by the priest «*Jos. Defranceschi*», names the godparents «*D. Joannes Bapta Defranceschi tricesimator ad S. Cosmam*» and «*Domicella Matthea Nobilis Josephi Thianich filia*»: a *tricesimator*, an officer of the *tricesima*, the Thirtieth, the customs on goods, at a place called St Cosmas. *doc*, read at full size and at the finest zoom on 3 November 2026. **That he is the deputy castellan and chamber officer who died at Crikvenica on 30 March 1801 is *inf*** (the same two Christian names, the same surname in the form the priest of Draga writes it, an office of the Chamber's service on the same coast, two years apart); it is not stated anywhere, and the entry of 1801 gives no office but the castellan's. **The office:** the Vinodol chamber castellany had its seat moved to Crikvenica in 1760 and was attached to the Hungarian Littoral in 1786 (the county's history of the lordships, moja-rijeka.eu); no list of its officials in the 1790s was found online. **A question, not an answer:** this archive's own Fiume record holds a *Joannes Baptista de Franceschi*, styled *D.nus*, a widower by 1771 when he married Catharina de Benzoni, with children indexed in 1773 and 1776 (see /fiume-1626/, the second household); a Benzoni family held offices in the Fiume captaincy in 1760, but nothing joins that Joannes Baptista to the man who died at Crikvenica, and the two may be unrelated. **That he is of this archive's name by descent is not established**, and nothing here says where he came from or whether he had children. *doc* for the words, read at full size and again at the finest zoom on 3 November 2026; the day numeral is blotted: the last digit reads 0 and the tens digit is a black blot, so the day 30 rests on the FamilySearch index of this entry (record Q2TW-C9YJ, 30 Mar 1801), not on the page. The entry stands between 14 January and 16 April 1801, in a book whose entries run in order. The entry was already in the FamilySearch index, which gives the name and the date and nothing more; the page, read on 3 November 2026 while walking the bundle, gives the words above. **⭐ Amended 5 November 2026: a second register entry of the same death.** The death book of Bribir (waypoint 9RKB-JWG, image 396, right page, folio 43, a reader's zoom of the entry, which I read myself) enters it as «*Obiit in Dno* **Nobilis ac Dnus Joannes Bapta Defranceschi, Dominalis Contrascriba, et Substitutus Castellanus Vinodolensis**, *Aetatis suae An: 49*, Crigvenicae, *ibidem ante Aram B.V. Rosariam tumulatus*», dated 30 March, year fixed by the sequence (1801). *doc* for those words. **New: his age, 49 (so born about 1751 or 1752); a second title, counter-scribe of the manor; and the burial, before the Rosary altar** (the Crikvenica entry says the cemetery). It still names no parent, wife or house, so **the question of who he is stays open**. What the same book adds is a widow «Catharina Defranceschi, nata Akacich», aged 65, who died on 7 December 1817 (image 468): told in the next two rows. That the 1801 deputy castellan is the Joannes Baptista who married Catharina Akacich at Bakar in 1772 is *inf*, resting on an age (49 in 1801, a bride of about 20 in 1772), on one Christian name and on a woman's maiden surname; the Gologorica Joannes Baptista (whom the tree dates 1752) has a wife née Sablich and is the other candidate. Not merged, not decided.
rows.where: FamilySearch, Crikvenica deaths 1798–1809 (waypoint 9RKB-DPD), image 351, page 11 · 3:1:939V-R99T-D8

rows.who: Vincentius Defranceschi, Nobilis (not an official: a student, found in the same book)
rows.what: «*Obiit in Dno omnibus SS. Sacramentis munitus* **Nobilis Vincentius Defranceschi**, *aetatis suae Annorum 16, mensium 9*, *et elapsis 48 horis sepultus est funus comitante hujate Ven. Capitulo*», the first entry on the page, with a small interlinear insertion above «aetatis suae» that reads «*Philosophiae* …» (the second word is Absolutus or Auditor; either way a student of philosophy, **unsettled**). The surname was zoomed at the finest level and is clear. Born about December 1781. **No parent is named, and nothing joins him to any household on the page**; the year is given by the heading «Anno 1798» two images before. *doc* for the words; his place in the family is open.
rows.where: FamilySearch, Bribir deaths from 1787 (waypoint 9RKB-JWG, roll 30), image 389, left page, folio 36

rows.who: Catharina Defranceschi, nata Akacich (a widow, not an official: found in the same book)
rows.what: «*obiit in Domino ex Senectute, & Morte naturali, Aetatis Annorum 65, omnibus Sacramentis munita* **Vidua Domina Catharina Defranceschi, nata Akacich**; *elapso tempore praescripto sepulta est per hoce Ven: Capitulum Bribiriense*». A widow, a gentlewoman, née Akacich, aged about 65 (born about 1752), buried by the Bribir chapter; no husband named. *doc* for the words. **What follows from them is inferred and not stated anywhere:** the only Catharina Akacich this archive knows is the bride of 20 November 1772 at Bakar, daughter of the late Antonius Akacich, who married Joannes Baptista, son of Franciscus Defranceschi; a woman of 65 in 1817 was 20 at that wedding, which fits a bride, so the widow is *probably* the 1772 bride and *possibly* the widow of the deputy castellan. That is a chain of two inferences and each is open: the Gologorica Joannes Baptista, whom the tree dates 1752, married Catharina Sablich at Bakar on 10 November 1783, so his wife was not an Akacich, and the man who died in 1801 could be either Joannes Baptista or a third. It also weakens the guess that the Catharina Defranceschi who died at Bakar on 7 April 1819 aged 85 is the bride: if the bride is the Bribir widow of 1817 she died two years before that, and the Bakar widow (born about 1734) is some other woman. Neither is established. **⭐ Amended 8 November 2026:** the baptism book of Novi Vinodolski names «*D. Catharina D. Joannis Baptistae De-franceski Contra-scribae Vinodolensis Consors*» as a godmother on 27 November 1795, beside **Antonius Akaich, canon of Bribir** (row below, image 418, zoomed): so the contrascriba's wife was a Catharina, *doc*, and the chain above, that the widow *nata Akacich* of 1817 was his widow, has one more link, the Akaich of Bribir at her side in 1795, which is a coincidence in a Bribir parish and not a statement; it stays *inf*.
rows.where: FamilySearch, Bribir deaths from 1787 (waypoint 9RKB-JWG, roll 30), image 468, right page, house no. 543

rows.who: Josephus De Franceski
rows.when: from 13 September 1798 to his death in September 1808; named 7 April 1804; named as dead by 16 February 1827
rows.what: **In his own hand he writes the name Defranceschi.** The baptism register of the parish of St Anthony at Draga (FamilySearch, Draga births, waypoint 9R28-PTY; the baptisms read so far begin in June 1796) was written by the parish priest *Aquinas Thian* until 1798, who from 28 May 1798 signs as administrator and from 13 September as *emeritus*; from **7 October 1798** the entries are written by «***Josephus Defranceschi, Pbrus Eccl. S. Antonij in Draga***» — *Pbrus* is *presbyter*, a priest, and he is not yet called *Parochus* in the entries of 1798 (he becomes *Parochus loci* in 1799) — and he signs nearly every entry on the next two images, to 9 January 1799, once as «*ego Jos. Defranceschi Pbrus loci ceremonias supplevi*» (the ceremonies of a baptism the midwife had already performed). *doc* for the first entry, image 17, left page, 7 October 1798 (a baby named Catharina, daughter of Michael and Antonia Vecerina): the surname is written «Defranceeschi», read at full size and at the finest zoom on 3 November 2026; the other entries to 9 January 1799 were read by an agent at normal view and have not been zoomed. In the same register he writes **«Parochus loci»** in full in some entries of 1799 (September, with «*Josephus De Franceschi Parochus loci*» on one of them), so the title of the Crikvenica entry is his own; and on **21 March 1799** the godfather at a baptism he performs is a **Joannes Baptista Defranceschi, tricesimator** (see the row above). **That this is the «Josephum De Franceski Parochum loci» of the Crikvenica death entry below is *inf***: the same parish, the same Christian name, the same office, six years apart, one clerk writing the name in the form the Crikvenica scribe heard it. Kin to anyone else of the name is **not established**. **The Crikvenica entry names him as the parish priest of the place at Draga** — «*provisus Smis Sacramentis per A.R.D. Josephum De Franceski Parochum loci*» — in the Crikvenica death entry of Petrus, son of Petrus Supan, who died aged 24 and about six months «*in Parochia ad Sctum Antonium Dragensi*» and was buried in «*Coemeterio communi Dragentium ad Claustrum Tersactense*», the common cemetery of the people of Draga beside the Trsat monastery. (The margin gives him a Crikvenica house, Kollor no. 85.) *A.R.D.* is *Admodum Reverendus Dominus*. **He is the priest of the Draga register for the whole stretch around 1804, in his own hand.** Images 25–56 of the same volume (1 July 1800 to 13 September 1808, folios 22 to 53; read by an agent at normal view, not zoomed) are one unbroken baptism book in which every entry opens «*Jos. Defranceschi Pchus loci baptizavit*» or «*Parochus loci*» (the surname written out in full, for instance on 7 August 1802 and on 4 July 1805, and in the first person on 13 July 1800, in May 1804, and on 6 June 1801, when he supplies the ceremonies of a baptism of necessity). The entries of February to June 1804 are all by him except that of 8 March 1804, baptised by a retired Capuchin parish priest of Fiume in the church of St Anthony, so on 7 April 1804, the day the Crikvenica scribe writes «*Josephum De Franceski Parochum loci*», the parish priest of Draga is, by the Draga book itself, the man who spells his name Defranceschi; the identification is still *inf*, because it rests on the name, the parish and the office and not on a shared document. **The Bakar marriage book names him once, as the priest of a Draga bride (29 January 1799).** The Bakar marriages (FamilySearch waypoint 9R28-82Z, image 207, left page, read on 5 November 2026 by a reader and zoomed by me at level 12): «*Die 29. Jan. Assistit matrimonio* [a groom of Bakar] *et Margaritae Barsovich e Parochia Draghensi, Draga A. R. D.* ***Josephus Defran-*** / *[ces]chi Parochus Draghensis, coram testibus Antonio Sablich et* …». The surname is split at the line end, «Defran-» clear and the rest at the start of the next line, so the ending is read, not seen whole. He stands as the priest of the bride's parish who gave her to the groom, on 29 January 1799, **twenty days after the last Draga baptism of his that the Draga book was read to (9 January 1799)** and here he is already called *Parochus* (*doc* for the words; the identity with the priest of the Draga register is *inf*, on name, parish and office). It adds no kin and no date of death. **He stops on 13 September 1808.** The last entries in his hand are of 3 July, 13 August, and 9, 12 and 13 September 1808 (image 56, left page, where «*Idem Parochus*» is his), the first of them with his name in full, «*Jos: Defranceschi Pchus loci sub conditione baptizavit*»; I looked at that page myself at normal view. From 21 September 1808 the entries are in other hands: first visiting friars («*V.P. Hyacinthus Rigetti Conc.*», then a Franciscan of the Trsat convent and a *P. Benedictus Dimmer*), and from 8 November 1808 **Bernardus, «Administrator Dragensis»**, who writes as «*Parochus ad S. Antonium in Draga*» from 1809 to the end of the images read (15 March 1810); he is, by name and office, the Bernardus of 1823 and the *Bernardus Xanich* of the 1837 schematism (*inf*). So the parish was without its priest from 13 September 1808. **How Xanich tells his own coming** (a reply to the magistrate of Bakar of 26 June 1834, draft and fair copy, images 139 right to 141 right; agent-read, with the dates zoomed by the agent): he came to Draga «*come Amministratore*» on 5 November 1808, was decreed «*effettivo Paroco, e Rettore*» by the Hungarian Lieutenancy Council on 22 «*9bre*» (November) 1808, received the bishop's collation on 31 January 1809, was installed on 12 February 1809, and on 24 February 1809 received from the Bakar magistrate, through the judge Giovanni Battista de Thianich and Giulio d'Orebich, «*i libri della Chiesa ofsigillati*», the church's books, **sealed**, and so crossed out that the churches seemed to hold no obligations (*doc*). That letter names none of his predecessors («*Predecessori M.M.R.R. Signori Parochi*», in the plural); a later one does. **He died in September 1808.** In a letter of 1841 to the archdeacon and parish priest of Bakar about the voluntary stole fees, Xanich writes that neither he nor «*meus Praedecessor Josephus Defranceschi*» had taken any fee for burials, «*qui hos minutos albae Stolae voluntarios a Populo proventus a 13tia Septembris 1798vi usque mensem Septembrem 1808vi sui Obitus, ego vero a 1a Novembris 1808vi*» (who had these small voluntary stole fees from the people **from 13 September 1798 until the month of September 1808, of his death**, and I from 1 November 1808, so for forty-three years in peaceful possession); the same words stand on the next page (images 154 right and 155 right of the Draga births volume; the first zoomed at level 13 by me on 4 November 2026, «sui Obitus» read with a long s, which the sense confirms; *doc*). So **Josephus Defranceschi was parish priest of Draga from 13 September 1798, the day Aquinas Thian's last entry is dated, until his death in September 1808**, the month in which the register stops carrying his name, 13 September 1808; Xanich, in other letters, gives his own arrival as 1 November (the Latin letters of 1836 and 1841) or 5 November 1808 («come Amministratore», the Italian draft of 1834), his decree as 22 November 1808, his oath and installation as 11 January 1809 before the bishop (1841) or his oath as 31 January and his installation as 12 February 1809 by the Bakar judge and the vicar general (1834): the letters do not agree on the days, and none of them gives a day for the death. **But the Draga marriage book gives a last living date: on 29 September 1808 he was still the parish priest and was hindered by illness.** Image 15, right page, of the Draga marriages (9R28-GPR, 3QS7-899X-R9M6-V), a marriage of that day by a Franciscan of the Trsat convent: «*Die 29 Sept. 1808 P. Ruffinus Czohar Ord. Min. Strict. Obs. … de licentia M.R.D. Parochi Dragensis, qui actu infirmitate fuerat praeditus* [*praepeditus*, hindered] *Josephi Defranceschi matrimonio junxit Joannem Bacarcich et Margaritham Bacarcich*», and the same friar's note below it, «*ob impotentiam Dni Parochi Dragensis*» («because of the incapacity of the parish priest of Draga»), the date word before «bris» a 7 or a 9, September by the order of the page (*doc*, zoomed by me at level 13, 4 November 2026). With Xanich's «until the month of September 1808, of his death» this puts his death in the last days of September 1808, unless Xanich's month is loose (*inf*); where he died and was buried is still not found. The two Draga marriage books (1797–1817 and 1815–1858, read on 4 November 2026, readers' pictures, not a «walked» claim) hold no other Defranceschi, Kovačina or Kalanj in any role: no wife, brother or relation of his marries or witnesses there. The third baptism book (1853–1858, with a confirmation list of 1874) holds none either; with it every Draga book on the FamilySearch film has been read for the three names (readers' pictures, none claimed walked), and his burial is not in any of them. Where he died and where he lay is not recorded: Xanich writes in 1841 that the Draga baptism and marriage registers run from 1790 but that **there is no death register before 1809**, «ob defectum Coemeterii», because the parish had no cemetery, and the note of 22 January 1818 says that the Draga dead were buried at Trsat and Bakar, so his burial entry, if one exists, is in the Trsat or the Bakar death book of September 1808 (*inf*). **His successor names him, in the same volume, as his predecessor, and as dead.** In the back of the Draga births volume Bernardus Xanich copied his own letters, and in one to the bishop of Senj and Modruš, «*Drago 16ta Februarii 1827*», signed «*Bernardus Xanich Parochus Dragensis*», he fears that debtors of the church will say, after his own death, that they had paid him, «*prout nonnulli dixere post mortem mei Praedecessoris Parochi defuncti Josephi Defranceschi*» (as some have said after the death of **my predecessor, the late parish priest Josephus Defranceschi**), and offers an extract of all the church's capitals since 1821 (*doc*: image 118, left page, lines 13–16, the name split «Defran-/ceschi» across the line break; read by an agent and zoomed at level 13 by me on 4 November 2026, «Josephi Defran-» clear). The same sentence stands twice more, in his petition to the Capitaneal Council of Bakar of «*Drage in Valle Bucarana die 20 Augusti 1830*», copied twice in a row (images 123 right and 124 right, read and once zoomed by an agent: «*meo Praedecessori defuncto Parocho Domino Josepho Defranceschi*», about debtors who, at the liquidation of 1820, said they had paid him). So **a parish priest of Draga named Josephus Defranceschi was Xanich's predecessor, and he was dead by 16 February 1827** (*doc*); the date and the place of his death are not given, and the Draga deaths filmed begin only in 1815 (9R28-GP5), the Crikvenica death book of 1798–1809 (above) holds no entry for him, and the note of 22 January 1818 (image 87) says that the Draga dead were buried at Trsat and Bakar, whose death books are the next place to look. That the man of the Draga register, of Xanich's letters and of the Crikvenica entry of 1804 is one and the same is *inf* from the name, the parish and the office; kin to the deputy castellan, or to the Crikvenica Defranceschi of this archive, is **not established**. Visiting clergy baptise now and then (the parish priest of Trsat, a Franciscan vicar of Trsat, a Capuchin, a canon of Bakar), always named in the entry. In all these images he is never a father, a godfather or a child: **no other Defranceschi, and no Kovačina or Kalanj, appears in the Draga baptisms from June 1796 to March 1810** except the godfather of 21 March 1799 above. A priest, then, of the same spelling, **three years after the deputy castellan, at a Draga where the Kovačina family of this archive also has a baptism, in 1849** (see /crikvenica-house/). Which Draga: the parish register of St Anthony at Draga (FamilySearch, Draga births 1785–1855, waypoint 9R28-PTY) is headed «*Pro Parochia ad S. Antonium in Valle Buccarensi*» and opens, on image 5, with a visitation decree of 16 June 1796 that names the place «*Vlaška Draga*»; that the Draga of this death entry is the same parish rests on the dedication to St Anthony and on the Trsat monastery's cemetery, so it is *inf*. **Which diocese, and how long a parish:** Draga lay in the diocese of Senj and Modruš, in its Buccari district, and the diocese's 1837 schematism says «*Parochia erecta anno 1789*» (the 1841 edition repeats it), so in 1804 the parish was fifteen years old and its priest one of its first. In 1837 the parish priest was «*Bernardus Xanich*»; a note dated 6 April 1823 on image 6 of the Draga births volume is written by a Bernardus as parish priest of Draga, so Josephus's time at Draga ended before 1823 (*inf*; the register itself shows it ended on 13 September 1808). The four Senj–Modruš schematisms that are online (1837, 1841, 1847, 1855) carry no *Franc-* name in a text search of the OCR, and none for 1800–1810 is online, so where he came from, and whether he was kin of the deputy castellan, is **not established**. *doc* for the words, read at full size and at the finest zoom on 3 November 2026. **Not in the Bakar death book:** the Bakar «Liber Mortuorum» 1773–1823 (waypoint 9R28-DPV, images 103–105) for August to December 1808 has no entry for a priest or for any Defranceschi (*doc*, level 12, read by me on 4 November 2026 for the months named only), so his burial place is still open: not Bakar in those months. Also unsettled whether he died at Draga, which had no cemetery of its own in 1808 by the record above, or elsewhere. **Trsat:** the Trsat death books on FamilySearch run 1737–1803 and then from November 1815 (waypoints 9R2F-ZNP, 9R2F-ZNG), so the book that would hold a Trsat burial of September 1808 is not on the film; his burial can be looked for there only at the parish or the state archive in Rijeka. **Answered 6 November 2026 by the Rijeka State Archives (*doc* for what they say; letter KLASA 611-03/26-42/2184, URBROJ 126-02-01/1-26-2, signed by the head, Markus Leideck; it reached David's e-mail on 9 November):** the archive «carried out the research» and found that in the death register of the parish of St George, Trsat, **no death of the said Josip Defranceschi, parish priest at Draga, is entered for 1803–1815**. It holds **digital copies** of that book and does not know where the original is kept. The Trsat friary had said on 5 November that the parish holds only post-war books. **What this is and is not:** a statement by the archive, giving no spellings tried, no pages and no entry numbers, so it is *their* nil, not one walked here (the digital copy has not been read by this archive); and a priest of Draga may be entered under another form of the name or under his office alone. His burial is therefore still not found: not Bakar (August–December 1808, read), not Trsat (per the archive), not Draga (no death book before 1815). **Draga's own death book** (waypoint 9R28-GP5) begins on 20 November 1815 and so cannot hold him; read end to end (to 11 April 1858, by readers from the page pictures, not claimed as walked), it names no Defranceschi, no Kovačina and no Kalanj, and shows that the parish had no cemetery of its own until a first burial in its own churchyard was blessed on 30 September 1855: before that the dead of Draga went to Trsat (by the Franciscan fathers) or to Bakar. His successor Bernardus Xanich is himself entered in it as dead on 25 February 1853, aged 74, buried at Trsat on 27 February (read by a reader, not zoomed). This makes the burial of 1808 at Trsat or Bakar likely (*inf*), and the Bakar book for August to December 1808 does not hold him; the Trsat book for 1808 is not on the film, and the Rijeka State Archives, which holds a digital copy, reports no entry for him in it (letter of 6 November 2026, above).

rows.who: Defranceschi names in the Bakar baptism book, 1773 – 1823 (godparents, one father; not officials)
rows.what: The baptism books of Bakar (Buccari) from 1770 to 1842 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R26-HZC, 594 images) were read on 5 November 2026, every page looked at once. **Every cell below was zoomed by me at level 13 unless I say otherwise.** The entries are told here in the order of the book. **(1) The household of Joannes Baptista and Catharina.** *Verification:* «Mariam Dorotheam, filiam D. Joannis Bapt. et Catharinae De Franciesch…» on 6 February 1773 (image 38, left) and «Antoniam fil. DD. Joannis Baptae Defranceschi et Catharinae», born on the evening of 7 January and baptised on 8 January 1776 (image 65, left) are the two baptisms the archive already held. **New:** on **25 December 1774** (image 52, right, the page headed «Nomina Baptizatorum 1774», entry 25) «*Antoniam Franciscam fil: leg: D. Joannis Bapta, et Catharinae* **Defrancesi**», baptised by a canon of the chapter, godparents named and none of the name. The Antonia buried at Bakar on 9 March 1775 (held already, told with the Bakar household) is, at ten weeks, *probably* this child, and the Antonia of January 1776 a second daughter given the same name; that is **inf**, and each is open. **(2) A girl, «Domicella Notburga Defranceschi», as godmother three times for certain and a fourth time contracted: 17 March 1785** (image 154, right, page 79, the line breaks after «Defran-» and goes on «-ceschi», both parts zoomed), **2 July 1788** (image 192, right, page 151, the first entry of July, the day figure cut by the margin; «Notburga Defranceschi:» across two zooms), **12 December 1788** (image 199, left, page 160, «Notburga Defran-» «ceschi») and **28 March 1789** (image 201, right, page 165, «Domicella Notburga Defranc…», the ending contracted; **not settled** as Defranceschi, so not counted). *Domicella* is the book's word for an unmarried girl. A **Nodburga Defranceschi** married **Joannes Verks** at Bakar on 27 February 1794 (held already, told with the Bakar household): the girl of 1785–89 is *probably* that bride (**inf**). Whose daughter she is, no entry says. The cells of Nothburga as a godmother in 1797–99 read Sambson, not Defranceschi, and are not counted. **(3) Vincentius.** 22 September 1786 (image 169, right, folio 107, entry 22): the godparents «*Dno Vincentio Defranceschi, et Domicella Maria ab Orebich*». A grown man in 1786, so **not** the Bribir student Vincentius who died on 10 September 1798 aged 16 (born about 1781), and nobody the archive holds. **(4) Joannes Baptista, and Joannes.** 4 August 1797 (image 230, right, page 221) the godfather is «*D. Joanne Bapta Defranceschi, et Catarina …ijch*» (the godmother's surname, a short word ending *-ich*, I do not settle); 17 July 1799 (image 233, left, page 226) the godfather is «*D. Joanne Defranceschi, et D. Ludovica Mariosc…rich*». The title *D.* is the one the Draga priest gives to the *tricesimator* Joannes Baptista Defranceschi on 21 March 1799 (told above); that the 1797 and 1799 godfathers are that man, and the deputy castellan who died at Crikvenica on 30 March 1801, is **inf**, with only the name and the coast to carry it. A «D. Joannes Baptista» who is *father* of children baptised on 6 May 1798 and 1 October 1799 has his surname unwritten in the cell and is **not counted**. **(5) Petrus.** 11 February 1801 (image 236, left, page 232) «*levant. Petro Defranceschi, et Katrina V.a Milletich*»; **2 September 1816** (image 299, left, folio 8, house 81) «*Petrus Def-ranceschi*», with Joanna, a widow, at the baptism of Maria, daughter of Lucas Franciscovich and Ursula; **25 September 1816** (image 300, left, folio 10, house 41) «*Pietro Defranceschy*», with a widow Maria Kopajtich, at the baptism of Cosmas, son of Stephanus and Margarita. The archive holds a **Petrus Defranceski, born 1772, who died at Bakar on 2 November 1818**; a man of 29 in 1801 and 44 in 1816 is *probably* he (**inf**). **(6) A father in 1823.** 13 August 1823 (image 370, right page, folio 150, the first entry, house 202): «*Antonius Josephus Ignatius, filius Dni Joann: Bapt: de Franceschi*, Cont: B'mo» (the cell after the name, a contraction, **not settled**), the mother «*Elisabeta nata de Carina*», the godparents Josephus and Antonia, a married couple of the Vignanin(i), *privati*; baptised by the abbot and parish priest. **A Joannes Baptista de Franceschi has a son at Bakar in 1823**, twenty-two years after the death of the deputy castellan of that name, so he is **not** that man; whether he is the Gologorica Joannes Baptista the tree dates 1752, or a younger man, no entry says. **Not counted** (seen and settled as other names): «Antonia Frances.» as godmother on 6 August 1776 and 7 September 1777, written with a stop and without a *De-*; a civis «*Josephus Franc…f*» with a wife Carolina née Porti on 24 January 1821 (zoomed, not De Franceschi); **Calampich** in 1783–84 (a reader's zoom, not Kalanj); one «Rukecina / Kukecina» godmother in February 1835 (a reader's zoom of the first letter, R or K, an *-cina* name that is not Kovačina). **What was not read as closely:** the chunks of images 216–221, 240–245 (the 1802–03 pages) and 486–491 (June 1833 to January 1834) were read at the supplied size without a zoom, so a Defranceschi in a godparent cell there could be missed. No Kovačina anywhere, and no Kalanj as a family; the one Kallanj is told on the [Kalanj page](/kalanj/).

rows.who: Franciscus Valentini De Franceschi, a godfather at Kraljevica (Porto Rè) in 1829 and 1831, styled Prior of the provincial lazaretto
rows.what: **A man of the name who held an office at the quarantine station of Kraljevica, found as a godfather twice.** The Kraljevica baptism book of 1815–1858 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2Z-VZ9) was read on 8 November 2026; two entries in it were zoomed by me at level 13. **(1) 12 July 1829** (image 57, left page, p. 106, entry 31, house 1): Margarita Catharina, a daughter of «*Anselmus filius Nicolai, et Veronicae Millich nata Sandrini, famulus ad prov. hocce Lazzarethum*» (a servant at the provincial lazaretto) and «*Maria nata Derotta*»; the godparents are «***D. Franciscus Valentini Defranceschi**, et Julia D. Antonii Facchinetti, uterque hujus Parochiae*», and the cell beside them, the *conditio*, begins «***Prior** ad hocce prov: **Lazzarethum***» and goes on «*filia chirurghi districtualis*…», the daughter of the district surgeon, which describes Julia (the rest of that line I do not read). The baptiser signs as Mathias Michaelis Mihicich, the royal chamber's parish priest at Porto Rè. **(2) 1 August 1831** (image 70, left page, p. 132, entry 26, house 1): Ignatius Loyola, a son of the same Anselmus and Maria née Derotta (the father again «*famulus ad hocce Regium prov. Lazzarethum*»); the godparents are «***Dni Franciscus Valentini De Franceschi** et Vincentia Dni Joannis Guthovich, utergue hujus Parochiae*» (the first letter of the last name is G or I), and the conditio reads «*Reg: **Prior** ad hocce prov: Reg: Lazzarethum, filia Vice-Consulis Gentis Romanorum*», the last words being Vincentia's. *doc* for the words: a **man of the name, in a royal post at the lazaretto of the Hungarian Littoral, in 1829 and 1831, of the parish of Kraljevica**. The two women are different, and **nothing in either entry says that either is his wife**; I do not write that she is. **Who he is is not said.** The only Francis of the right age whom this archive holds as the son of a Valentin is the child baptised at Fiume on 17 June 1797 to Valentinus and Ursula (see the household above); he would be thirty-two in 1829, and the name and the patronymic fit, so that is **inf** and no more: the register gives no age, no birthplace and no parent. The port captain Ferencz Defranceschi, below, is on the Hungarian state's lists from about 1814 and the same warning stands over him: nothing says that he and this Prior are one man, and a lazaretto is not the harbour master's office. Facchinetti and Guthovich are Kraljevica names read from the same two entries; they are not our target surnames and are not added to any catalogue. **The rest of the book** (baptisms from November 1815 to 12 February 1858, every image looked at once by readers on 8 November 2026) gave **no other cell of the name**, so these are the only two; no Kovačina and no Kalanj stands in the book either, and a few cells are unsettled and named in the [row of the volume](/searched/). The births after 12 February 1858 are on the next roll (56), which is not opened.

rows.what: **The Trsat baptism book names a man of the name as the head of the lazaretto of St Francis at Martinščica, in the Hungarian Littoral, from 1834 to 1845, and gives him five children.** The Trsat baptisms (FamilySearch, waypoint 9R2C-VZH, «Liber V Baptizatorum», images 3–143, and «Liber VI», 150–224; read on 8 November 2026 by readers, every image once; the cells below were **zoomed by me at level 13 unless I say otherwise**) hold these entries. **(1) The prior's children and his one godfathership.** **6 December 1834** (image 89, right page, p. 173, the first entry): «*Andrinam Juliam Carolinam Franciscam filiam legitimam Domini Francisci, et Catharinae jugalium **Defranceschi** Lazaretti S. Francisci pr. Martinschizza* [the rest of the line, read at level 12:] *p. Prioris*», born 2 December, baptised in the lazaretto chapel by the lazaretto's chaplain Cajetanus Kobler; the godparents (level 12) are Franciscus Bassan, a Fiume merchant, and Carolina, widow of Andreas Bellinich, a Fiume patrician; the parish priest Josephus Visner signs «Vidi». **27 December 1834** (image 89, right, the fourth entry, house cell «Martinschizza»): the child of another couple, baptised by Kobler by the parish priest's special delegation, the godfather «*Perillustri Domino Francisco **Defranceschi** Regii Lazaretti S. Francisci* [level 12:] *in Martinschizza Littorali hungarico siti, provisorio Priore*» and Ursula Glasar. **7 June 1836** (image 96, left, p. 186, the first entry): «*Ludovicum Vincentium Carolum Franciscum filium legitimum Domini Francisci, et Catharina jugalium **Defran-ceschi** Lazarethi S. Francisci prioris*», baptised in the lazaretto (the godparents, a Fiume official of the Tribunal of Exchange and the Health Office and a «domicella Anna de Bonzoni», are a reader's reading, not zoomed). **[February] 1838** (image 104, right, p. 201, the last entry, house cell «Martinschiza», the day cell «D.° die 22», the month and year read from the page by a reader as 22 February 1838): «*Carolinam Iginiam Samuelam Juliam filiam legitimam Domini Francisci **Defranceschi**, et Catharina **Bellinich** jugalium, Levantibus Domino Iginio Scarpa Patritio Fluminensi, et Domina Carolina Vidua Bellinich, nec non qua teste Domino Samuele* [Hair?] *… die 16 currentis natam in Capella Lazzareti S. Francisci, impedito Adm Rdo Dno Cajetano Kobler ejusdem Capellano, ego Josephus Visner*…» (the baby was born in the lazaretto chapel on the 16th). **27 January 1844** (image 129, right, p. 251, the last entry, house cell «Susak»): «*Carolum Andream … filium legitimum Spectabilis Domini Francisci De-fran|**cheski** Priori R: Lazzarethi S. Francisci, et Domina Catharina nata **Bellinich** Conjugum, baptizavit Andreas Rubi[s]a(?) R: Gymnasii Flum: II Gramm: prof: p. O. de licentia, Levantibus patrini Francesco Spadoni, et Domina Carolina Bellinich Vidua, natum 20ma hujus vespere hora 7½*» (the ending «-cheski» and everything after it zoomed; the beginning «De-fran» read by a reader; the spelling with *ch* and the Slavic *-ski* is new to the catalogue and is added to it). **23 February 1845** (image 134, right, p. 261, the first entry, house cell «Tersat»): «*Franciscam Juliam Georgiam filiam legitimam Domini Francisci **Defranceschi**, et Catharinae natae **Bellinich** jugalium*», born 16 February, baptised by Kobler, «Lazzarethi in Martinschiza Capellanus»; the godfather, Franz de Rauhmüller, a royal councillor, is represented by a Fiume merchant (a reader's reading). So the prior has a wife **Catharina née Bellinich** and children baptised in the lazaretto chapel in **1834, 1836, 1838, 1844 and 1845** (*doc* for all five; the children of 1834 and 1844 are new to this archive). **(2) Four godparents of the name, 1818–1827, none of them the prior by any word in the entry.** **14 June 1818** (image 16, left, p. 26, entry 23): the godfather «***Valentino De franceschi***», *conditio* «**Civilista**», at the baptism of Antonia, daughter of Matthaeus (the surname a reader reads Stiedenak) and Lucia; a second godparent, a woman, stands below him with a name that begins «Franchesche» and is not settled. **20 May 1819** (image 21, left, p. 36, entry 23): the same couple's Hellena; the second godmother, a woman whose first name is Antonia, stands «*in vece dello Sr **Joseffo De franceschi***, Civilista», that is, she is his proxy (the last line cut by the crop at level 13 and read on the whole page at level 12). **4 March 1820** (image 26, left, p. 46, entry 11, house 8): at the baptism of Antonia Elena Francisca, daughter of Antonius Sirola and Cattarina, the godparents are Antonia David and «***Francesco Defranceschi***», *conditio* «**Reg.º Impiegato**», a royal official. **8 September 1827** (image 60, right, p. 175, the third entry, house cell «Susak»): at the baptism of Anna Maria, daughter of the coachman Franciscus Colazio and Theresia, the godparents are «***Franciscus Defranceschi***», *conditio* «**R. Impiegatus**», and Anna de Benzoni, *Possidente*. **Who they are is not said**, and the register gives no relationship. *Inferred, and no more:* the Franciscus of 1820 and 1827, a royal official, and the prior of 1834–1845 may be one man, and may be the port captain **Defranceschi Ferencz** of the Hungarian lists, below, and the Prior «*Franciscus Valentini De Franceschi*» of the lazaretto at Kraljevica in 1829 and 1831, above (the same Christian name and the same office on the same coast, at Kraljevica in 1829–31 and at Trsat in 1834–45); the Valentino of 1818 may be the Valentinus of Fiume who married in 1793 and died in 1839 (held above), and the «Franciscus Valentini» of 1829 his son. None of that is stated in any entry, and each link is open. **What this does to a card on this page.** The household «Franciscus × Catharina Bellinich» (h064, the card with the place label «Bakar (Vitipolis)» for 1836) was built from the FamilySearch index only: the register shows that the children of 1836, 1838 and 1845 were baptised in the chapel of the lazaretto and entered at **Trsat**, and that a prior's family of five children had its house at Martinščica from 1834; whether the place label is the index's or the family's, I have not settled and have not edited that card. **Not counted:** Francesco, Franciscus and Franz as a given name beside other surnames; a godfather «Franciscus Defeso…t» (image 27, right, p. 49, entry 27, 18 June 1820) whose surname is unsettled. **(3) A chancellor of the Health Office at Rijeka, 1850.** **14 August 1850** (Liber VI, **image 175, right page, p. 49, entry 53**, house cell «Podvežica»; zoomed by me at level 13, the whole entry): «*Annu Franku kćer Jurja Paškvan težaka, i Ursule rođene Marać — kum bi **G. Franjo Defrančeski, Kancilier Sanitota u Rike**, i Gna Anna Oliva rođ. Zonković — krstih ja plovan Žuvičić*» (the child, Anna Franka, was born the day before; *doc* for every word). A man «Franjo Defrančeski» whose office is *Kancilier Sanitota u Rike* (the chancellor of the health office, the *Sanità*, at Rijeka) stands godfather at Podvežica. **Who he is the entry does not say.** *Inferred, and no more:* he may be the Franciscus of 1820 and 1827 and the prior of the lazaretto of 1834–1845 (both held posts in the quarantine and health service, and the baptiser, a Croat, writes the name in the Slavic form in which the prior's child of 1844 is written, «Defran-/cheski»), but nothing in the entry says so. **(4) A godmother «Marija Defranci», 1855–1856, unmarried.** **29 April 1855** (Liber VI, **image 208, left page, p. 114, entry 30**, house cell «Selo br. 80»; zoomed by me at level 13): «*Pilipa rođjena danas sina zakonskog Jakova Kamenar nadničara, i Marie Fučat — krstio plovan P. Žuvičić. Kumi biahu: Fran Prešić Kalafat, i **Maria Defranci**, oba neoženjeni*» (the child Pilip, born that day; the surname is plainly **Defranci**, the last stroke a flourish; *doc*). The same name, read by a reader at crop size and **not zoomed**: **2 August 1856** (image 216, left, p. 130, entries 40–41, house «Trsat br. 13», the twins Elizabeta and Marija of Josip Kolacio, a butcher, and Marija Glažar), godmother «Marija Defvanci» (the third letter from the end read as v, probably r), and **12 October 1856** (image 217, right, p. 133, entry 68, «Pećine br. 9»), the godparents «Jože Dobre i Marija Defranci». No parent of the name stands in the 1850–1860 pages, and no priest. She may be a daughter or niece of the chancellor, or of the prior; the entries give no relationship, and **that is not said anywhere**. **What this does to a card on this page:** nothing is changed; the five children of the prior's household (h064, 1834–1845) were baptised at Trsat while the father was prior; what became of the family after 1845 is not in the Trsat baptisms read so far (no further child of the prior in 1850–September 1860). **(5) A mother «Dominica Defranca», 1863.** **Image 345, left page, page 113, entry 73** (zoomed by me at level 13): «*Die 3a Decembris 1863 — 6a — Nicolaus — illegitimus — **Dominica Defranca**, Coelebs, ex Istria, Ancila*», the house on the right page «Sušak 8» (read by a reader), the baptiser Paschalis Žuvičić: **an unmarried servant from Istria, whose surname is written Defranca, has an illegitimate son Nicolaus at Sušak**; no father is named, nothing else is said (*doc*). The ending -a is feminine or Istrian; it is added to the Atlas catalogue as an attested form with the place, the year and the kind of record only. **No relationship to any person above is stated, and none is inferred.** **What was not read:** the pages after 25 January 1867 (the register goes on, on the next roll, 130), and the repeats of the pasted-slip pages; the death of the Ludovicus of 1836 (which the card gives as 1 June 1855) would be in the death book. **Images 144–149 are slates and covers; 225–231 are a blank leaf, slates and the cover and title leaf of the 1858 book; 403–407 are end slates.**

rows.who: Antonia de Franceschi, a godmother at Novi Vinodolski in 1695, «of Rijeka» (not an official: found in the Novi baptism book)
rows.what: **A woman of the name, called Signora and «of Rijeka», as godmother in the oldest baptism book of Novi Vinodolski.** The Novi Vinodolski volume of 1650–1804 (FamilySearch waypoint 9RK1-3Y7, roll 217) was begun on 8 November 2026; the first Defranceschi-type cell in it is on **image 51, left page, the second entry of the page** (the entries are not numbered, the left page carries no number; the right page is numbered 47), written by Pop Thoma Mariassevich: «*Na 4 8bra. Kersti Gdin Pop Thoma Mariassevich Bartolu Kargacinu heker imenom Franciskinu Margaritu od njegove zakone xene Kattarine roienu: kum bi Jacinto Peri kuma **Sig:ra Antonia de Franceschi od Rike***». The baby is the daughter of Bartol Kargacin and Katarina; the godfather is Jacinto Peri (the Peri family of the book, who use *Francesco* only as a given name); the godmother is a *Signora*, «*od Rike*», of Rijeka. **Zoomed by me at level 13 (*doc*): «de Franceschi», the particle apart, the last letters *-schi* or *-sci* (the tail of the word is a long s, a c and a short stroke before the final i; both are forms in the Atlas's Defranceschi catalogue).** The year is not written on the entry: the page before it (image 50, right, folio 56/46) is headed *1695* and the page after it (image 51, right) is headed *1696*, and the entries between run from September to December, so **4 October 1695** is read from the headings (*doc* for the sequence; no other year heading intervenes). **Who she is is not said**: no husband, no parents, no house; that she belongs to the Fiume family of the name is *inf* at most (the same name, the same town, a godmother's rank), and nothing here links her to a household of this archive. It is the **earliest cell of the name in any Vinodol book read so far**, and the first at Novi; the rest of the volume is being read in sixes by readers and the row of the whole volume will say which part is read.
rows.where: Novi Vinodolski (godmother «od Rike», of Rijeka)

rows.who: Defranceski, a «porkulab», and a lady of his house, as sponsors at the Novi Vinodolski confirmations of July 1770 (not named: found in the Novi confirmation lists)
rows.what: **Two sponsors of the name in one visitation, one a man called «Porkulab De Franceski» and one a woman called «Porkulabicza de Franceski».** The Novi Vinodolski volume (FamilySearch waypoint 9RK1-3Y7, roll 217) binds, between its death book and the births of 1784, the parish's lists of the confirmed (*Birmani*), written in Croatian in Latin letters, one line to a person, «*X son of Y, k. Z*» (*k.* is *kum*, sponsor). The list of 1770 opens «**1770 Dan 18 ij 19 Jula**», the days of the first holy visitation of the bishop, whose name is written «*Pio De Manzado[r]*» as the readers have it (I read the heading at page size only). **(1) Image 347, left page (the men's list), the line after «*Martin Franka Maricichia, k. Dusko Kargachin*»:** «*Alberto Ivana Kargachina, k. P. Porkulab De Franceski.*» **(2) Image 349, right page (pencil numbers 435 and 345), the first line under the heading «Divojcicze» (the girls' list):** «*Elisabetha Waugenheber, k. Gpa Porkulabicza de Franceski.*» *doc*: both lines **zoomed by me at level 13**, the surname read whole in each (*De Franceski* with a capital D and the particle apart in the first, *de Franceski* in the second; a long *F*, *-ceski* with a plain *s*). The boy is a son of Ivan Kargachin (a Novi family of the book); the girl's surname is written *Waugenheber*. **What the word is.** *Porkulab* is, I take it, the Croatian form of the Hungarian *porkoláb* and the German *Burggraf*, the warden or castellan of a castle; *Gpa* is *gospoja*, a lady, and *-ica* the Croatian ending that makes a wife of a man's title, so the second line is the lady of the *porkulab* of the name. **That reading of the word comes from the dictionary, not from the page, and is *inf*; the *P.* before it is an abbreviation that I do not expand (the lines around it use *P.* before the names of captains, priests and townsmen).** **What it is worth.** The Vinodol dominion had a castellan, and the man who died at Crikvenica on 30 March 1801 was «*Dominalis Contrascriba, et Substitutus Castellanus Vinodolensis*» (the first row of this page, and the row about his wife below): a *porkulab* of the same surname in the same dominion **twenty-five years earlier** is, *inf*, an officer of that service, and the nearest thing to a written beginning of the family's office here. **That the porkulab of 1770 is Joannes Baptista, or his father, or kin of him, is not said anywhere**: no given name is written, and a man who was 49 when he died in 1801 was 18 in 1770. It is the oldest cell of the name *De Franceski* in any Vinodol book read so far, written by a Croatian hand with the ending *-ski* that this archive's own Crikvenica family uses from the 1860s. Nothing links him to Antonia of Rijeka in 1695, above.
rows.where: FamilySearch, Novi Vinodolski, confirmation lists bound in the volume of 1650–1804 (waypoint 9RK1-3Y7, roll 217), images 347 (left) and 349 (right)

rows.who: Catharina, wife of Joannes Baptista De Franceski, contrascriba of the Vinodol, a godmother at Novi Vinodolski in 1795 (not an official: found in the Novi baptism book)
rows.what: **«D. Catharina D. Joannis Baptistae De-franceski Contra-scribae Vinodolensis Consors»: the wife of the contrascriba, with her name, in a register.** In the Novi Vinodolski baptism book of 1784–1804 (FamilySearch waypoint 9RK1-3Y7, roll 217), **image 418, right page (p. 85), the entry of house no. 277, «Die 27ma», among the baptisms of November 1795** (the year 1795 is not written on the entry: it is inferred from the span of the six images, 17 August 1795 to 9 December 1796), the cooperator baptised **Vincentia**, the child of Joannes Kergaein, son of Joannes, and Luciana, born Pisku(l)ich, of the parish. The godparents are «*D. Stit.[?] Antonius Akaich Can[onicus] à Latere D. Illmi Ordinarij, et Coll[egiatae] Bribiriensis, et D. Catharina D. Joannis Baptistae De-franceski Contra-scribae Vinodolensis Consors*». The line breaks after *De-*. *doc*: **zoomed by me at level 13**; every word of the godmother's description is plain, the surname in the form *De-franceski* with the *-ski* ending, as in the Crikvenica death entry of 1801 and at Novi in 1770 (above). A reader at normal size found the cell and read it the same way. **What it gives.** The wife of the man who died at Crikvenica on 30 March 1801 as «*Dominalis Contrascriba, et Substitutus Castellanus Vinodolensis*» (first row, with the Bribir entry) is, in November 1795, **Catharina**, and her husband is called *Contrascriba Vinodolensis* with the same words the Bribir clerk uses for him five years later: *doc* for the words, and that the contrascriba of 1795 and the man of 1801 are one is *inf* with the title, the dominion, the names and the surname in the same form to carry it, and nothing against it. **Beside her stands a canon of Bribir, Antonius Akaich.** The only Catharina this archive has put next to the name and to a Bribir grave is the widow *nata Akacich* buried by the Bribir chapter in 1817 (row below) and the bride of 1772 at Bakar, daughter of the late Antonius Akacich: **that the godmother of 1795 is that Catharina, and that the canon is of her family, is a guess that two coincidences (the Christian name, and an Akaich of Bribir at her side) now make better and that no entry says**; the entry names no kinship. The Draga entry of 1799 (first row) puts a *tricesimator* of the same names at the font of Draga; this is the first cell of the name at a font to come with a wife, and the first of the contrascriba at Novi.

rows.who: Joannes Defrancesci, a godfather at Jablanac in 1810, with a title ending «-tore» (not named as an official: found in a note at the foot of a Novi Vinodolski baptism page)
rows.when: baptism of 10 May 1810, entered in the Novi book
rows.what: **A «D. Defrancesci Joanne» as a sponsor at Jablanac in May 1810, in a note written under the entries of Novi Vinodolski.** The second Novi Vinodolski volume (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2M-82L, births 1804–1852), **image 52, right page (p. 253, folio 127), at the very foot, under the last entry of 15 May 1809** (the baptism of a child of Adamus Merzljak and Margaretha née Kukalj), in a later, smaller hand: «*Parochus Jablanacensis Lucas Potochnijak baptizavit in Jablanac Mariam filiam Mathai et Barbara Potochnijak jugalium, levantibus **D. Defran-** / **cesc?i Joanne D.º 3?tore** et Hellena Turina die 10ª Maij 1810. ita delatum Parocho Stanislao Czar…*»: the priest of Jablanac baptised Maria, daughter of Matthaeus and Barbara Potochnijak, at Jablanac, and the sponsors were *D. Defran-cesc?i Joannes* and *Hellena Turina*; the entry was then reported (*delatum*) to the parish priest of Novi, Stanislaus Czar, who has it written here. *doc*: **zoomed by me at level 13.** *Defran-* ends the line, plain; the next line opens with a colon-like mark and *cest?i* (the fourth letter is *c* or *t*; I read *Defrancesci*, a form the Atlas holds, and the join over the line is the only thing between the word and the name); *Joanne* is plain. After *Joanne* come an abbreviation *D.º* (or *R.º*) and a word that begins with the figure **3** and ends *-tore*, with a second figure that I read as an *8* or a *0* and cannot settle at this size. **What it may be, and what it is not.** If the figure is a *0*, the word is «*30tore*», **tricesimator** (*trigesimatore*), an officer of the *tricesima*, the customs: the same office that the Draga baptism of 21 March 1799 gives to a *D. Joannes Bapta Defranceschi tricesimator ad S. Cosmam* (first row of this page). That is a reading of one figure, *inf*, and the entry says nothing else of his work. **He is not the Joannes Baptista who died at Crikvenica in 1801:** nine years separate them, and the note gives no second name, no wife, no parent and no age. It may be the same man's son, brother or kinsman, a second officer of the name, or a man unrelated to either; nothing here decides. The note is not one of the Novi births (the child was baptised at Jablanac, a place on the coast south of Senj): it stands in a register that is not the one it is about. **What is not established:** the first letter of the title (*D.* or *R.*), the second figure, the fourth letter of the surname, and the last word of the note after *Czar*.

rows.who: The Bakar baptism book, 1843 – 1884: no Defranceschi baptism, one marginal note of 1948; the Kovačina and the Kalanj told elsewhere
rows.when: the register of 1843 – August 1884; a marginal note of 9 October 1948
rows.what: The baptism book of Bakar (Buccari) for 1843–1884 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2C-L23, 530 images; the volume that follows the one told in the row above) was read on 5 November 2026, every register page looked at once, images 8–528. **No Defranceschi, De Franceschi or Franceski in any role of any baptism (child, parent, godparent, baptiser), and no priest Josephus Defranceschi.** **One later note names a Franceski.** In the remarks column of an entry of **August 1880** (image 458, right page, page 634, entry 76, a girl born on 15 and baptised on 18 August 1880, Krasica gornja 108), a modern hand writes, in Croatian, «*Sklopila ponovni ženitbu sa Valentin* **Franceskom** *u Fiume 9.X.1948 (u sp. br. 148/1948)*» — «she married again, to Valentin Franceskom, at Fiume on 9 October 1948». I read the surname at level 13 as **Franceskom**, the instrumental of *Franceski*; the *e* and *s* are cramped, and *Francelom* is not wholly excluded. *doc* for the note, *inf* for the reading and for the name. It is a Rijeka marriage of 1948 recorded in the margin of a baptism of 1880, so it points to the civil marriage register of Rijeka of 1948 (the number 148/1948) and not to this archive's lines; nothing else about him is known here. **The Kovačina and the Kalanj of the same book are told where they belong:** a finance guard **Thomas Kovacsina** with a daughter on 13 March 1847, and a **Petar Kovačina** as a witness on 31 August 1868 (both told in the two rows that follow, and the name on the [Crikvenica house page](/crikvenica-house/)); a **Barić couple**, a finance official and an Antonia Kalanj, in 1855–57, and **two Kalain godparents** of Višnjevica in 1876 (on the [Kalanj page](/kalanj/)). **Not counted** (seen and settled as other names): Franciskovic (hundreds of entries), Franelić, Smokvina, Kovacić / Kovačević (a layman's name), Fiandrini / Findini, Depauli, Voncina (a godfather of 1873–74 and 1880, zoomed: a V), Kalafat (a trade), Marochini, Calampich; a patronymic «francesci» of 12 May 1869 (image 324, entry 51) and a father «Arsenio» with Francesci as a patronymic (image 366, entry 97, zoomed by a reader). Draga is named as a place of godparents and in later notes (1866 to 1884), and Rijeka many times; neither is a family.
rows.where: FamilySearch, Bakar births 1843–1884 (waypoint 9R2C-L23), image 458 R (the note of 1948), images 38 R, 111 R, 124 L, 315 R, 404 R

rows.who: Thomas Kovacsina, a finance guard, at Bakar — a daughter baptised 13 March 1847
rows.what: **Two years before the baptism of Petar at Draga, the same name and the same trade at Bakar.** The Bakar (Buccari) baptism book of 1843–1857 (FamilySearch waypoint 9R2C-L23, image 38, right page, page 60, entry 35, read on 5 November 2026 and zoomed at level 13) baptises, on **13 March 1847**, «*Josepham*» the daughter of the spouses «*Thomae* **Kovacsina** *Vigiliarum financialium Vigilis, et Maria nata Jakovcich*» — a guard of the finance watch and his wife Maria, née Jakovcich; the baptiser is Joannes Soich, administrator of the parish; the godparents are Joannes Matessich, a guard, and Joanna Rossich. The surname is underlined and written *Kovacsina* in full. *doc* for the entry. **That this Thomas is the Tome Kovačina «servant of the finance» of Draga in 1849 and the «Defct. Thomas Kovačina, custos financialis» of the widow's death entry of 1877 is *inf***: the same surname, the same Christian name, the same service, the same wife's first name, two years and one parish apart on the same coast; the finance posted its guards from station to station, and Bakar–Draga–Crikvenica is a plausible run of postings. **What does not fit yet:** the wife's maiden name is *Jakovcich* here and *Sko·ić* on the page of the Draga baptism of 29 June 1849 (read at level 13 on 5 November 2026, Draga births image 290, right page, page 121: an S, k, o, then smeared letters crossed by a descender from the line below, and an ending *-ić*; the FamilySearch index has «Skovich»; there is no *Jak-* in it), and the widow of 1877 has no maiden name in her death entry; the two surnames are not the same word, so either one of them is a misreading or they are two women, and no entry decides which; that is one point against the identification of 1847 with 1849, which rests now on the surname, the Christian name and the trade only. Josepha is not found again in the pages this archive has read; she is open. The same book names no other Kovačina before 1868 except an open genitive «Kovain / Kovacin-a» of 4 December 1853 (image 96), which is the stem *Kovačin*, not *Kovačina*, and is not counted (see the next row).
rows.where: FamilySearch, Bakar births 1843–1884 (waypoint 9R2C-L23), image 38, right page

rows.who: Petar Kovačina, a witness at Bakar, 31 August 1868
rows.what: **A «Petar Kovačina», written out with the caron, signs as a witness at Bakar.** In the same book (image 315, right page, page 353, entry 91, a girl, Augustina Rosa, born on 28 and baptised on **31 August 1868**, the baptiser Joannes Balas, cooperator; zoomed at level 13 on 5 November 2026) the remarks column reads, in a Croatian hand, «*Ojzdelic Martin / Mate Bicepeg svedoci / **Petar Kovačina** svedok*» — three witnesses, the third Petar Kovačina; the line looks like a witnessed note on the illegitimate child's parentage, and what it attests is not read here. *doc* for the name on the page. **Whether this is Petar the elder is *inf* only:** Petar of Draga, baptised on 29 June 1849 as the son of a finance guard, would be nineteen in the summer of 1868 and living some miles from Bakar; the name and the age fit, and nothing else in the entry says who he is, his trade, his father or his place. It is the first sighting of a **Petar Kovačina before the Crikvenica registers** and is kept as a lead.

rows.who: A child of Susak in 1844 whose parents' surname is written De Francesci (not an official: found in the Trsat death book and its index)
rows.when: died 2 February 1844 (the register) or 2 January 1844 (the index)
rows.what: The death book of Trsat (Tersatto), whose parish held Susak, the hamlet across the Rječina from Rijeka, was read for the three names on 5 November 2026, every page once (1815 to 1857), and so was the parish's death index. **The register (image 63, right, the page headed «Januario 1844», house column «Susat»):** «***Carolus*** *filius leg. Francisci, et Catha-rina* **De Franc…i** *jugalium*», 13 days, «*Ex atrophia, sepultus post 30 horas*». A reader and I first read the child's name as *Paulus*; at level 13 the first letter is a C and the word is **Carolus**, and the first reading is withdrawn. The last syllables of the surname are a flourish. **The index (the letter D, page 16, FamilySearch waypoint 9RKB-82Q, image 19, right):** «**DeFrancesci** *Carolus filius leg. Francisci, et Catharina jug. die 2. Jan. 844. 13 Dies*» (zoomed at level 13). The copyist writes the surname plainly *De Francesci*, the Italian *-sci* for the *-schi* of **Defranceschi**, and the register's flourish fits it. The two books agree on everything but the month (the register «Februarii die 2», the index «Jan»); which of the two is the slip I do not settle. **The second entry that a reader gave as a Defranceschi is not one.** A girl, «*Margarita filia leg. Francisci, et Elisabetha jug.*», died 24 February 1844, aged four days; the word before her name begins *De-p-r-e-* and the index writes it **Depreda** on the row beneath Carolus, a family that has other entries at Susak. Withdrawn. So what the books hold is **one child, Carolus, whose parents Franciscus and Catharina bear the name De Francesci at Susak in the winter of 1844** (*doc* for the words; *inf*, and open, that the name is ours). Nothing links Franciscus to the Bakar or Rijeka households on this page. It matters because the Bakar father of 1849 is entered «Defranceschi Regii» (Franciscus) and Susak is the next town to Rijeka. The index also holds **Defranceschi Antonija, 70, 22 December 1899**, who is already on this archive's roster (1829–1899, from the burial record): a second witness to the death, nothing new. The same books write **Defei / Deffei** at Susak (1826, 1848: a different name, zoomed) and **Covacich**, **Smokvina** and **Margan**; none of them is ours.
